hotspots.title: Vibe-coding platforms move into enterprise private clouds
hotspots.summary: AWS now allows vibe-coding tool Superblocks to be embedded into the private clouds of AWS customers, signaling that enterprise buyers want low-code/vibe-coding development inside their own infrastructure, decoupled from any single model provider.
chase_rationale: Enterprise adoption of vibe-coding tools inside private cloud environments
Model decoupling trend has procurement and governance implications

samples.title: AWS is helping vibe-coding startup Superblocks, and the implications are big

hotspots.title: AI agents as scheduled maintenance workers: nightly rebase-and-verify workflows
hotspots.summary: David Crawshaw's widely-quoted prompt describes a nightly cron job where an AI agent fetches upstream changes, rebases local modifications, verifies the software still works, and replaces the current version - a template for reliable autonomous dependency and update maintenance.
chase_rationale: Shows a concrete, verifiable pattern for agentic software maintenance
High relevance for platform teams designing autonomous update workflows

hotspots.title: Open-source devtools argument intensifies as AI coding tooling matures
hotspots.summary: Simon Willison highlights the 'Devtools must be open source' argument (exe.dev), emphasizing that when AI agents take over code examination and modification, developers lose the freedom to inspect and modify the tools themselves unless devtools remain open source.
chase_rationale: Open-source governance angle directly affects developer tool procurement
Raises trust and auditability concerns for AI-powered devtools
